messages.text:
Very interesting pics and so quickly put together. 
West pier has a particular significance in my life. I lived opposite in our family hotel from the age of 16. I watched the landing station fall into the sea with my brother. My mum was a save the west pier society member and campaigned for it to be saved for 40 years. They use to try and sell it to the right investor for £1 but wealthy investors were often turned down such as a Disney land. A underwater maze and recreating a Victorian feel were popular but never happened. Some argue that the purists limited the chances of its survival. We scattered my Mum and Dad’s ashes there so I like to feel they enjoyed an ashes surfer’s party with the dolphins. Feel free to put this memory on your creation inspired by it. Bx

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from Argus readers' Facebook group, “We grew up in Brighton”: “I remember The West Pier where my nana and mum would take me and they would have tea dances at the far end of the pier.” — Anne T. https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/18661633.argus-readers-share-memories-growing-brighton/

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from Argus readers' Facebook group, “We grew up in Brighton”: “I fondly remember the glass animal man in Queen’s Road and playing on the Victorian slot machines on the West Pier.” — Gina N. https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/18661633.argus-readers-share-memories-growing-brighton/

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from Argus readers' Facebook group, “We grew up in Brighton”: “I used to walk on the West Pier and go to the paddling pool and picnic with my mum, happy child hood memories.” — Ann R. https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/18661633.argus-readers-share-memories-growing-brighton/

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from the blog It's all about the photos, 2011: “I wish I'd taken more time to admire it like I do now. I still think West Pier is beautiful.” — PhotoPuddle. http://itsallaboutthephotos.blogspot.com/2011/09/swarming-over-west-pier-by-tommy-martin.html

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from a letter in The Argus: “I remember spending many happy days as a child on the wonderful West Pier so I was very sad to see it finally collapse into the sea.” — Edith H. https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/5117156.too-late/

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from BBC News Talking Point, 3 January 2003: “I remember walking on the pier in the early 70's and feel very optimistic about its future. It is an integral part of our city.” — Martin. http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/talking_point/2617507.stm

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from a blog comment on Clive A.'s “Better Than Any Screensaver”, 2007: “Done it meself stood Waiting for a bus watching the birds Fly, Only to miss the Bus. Is easy to get transfix by the dancers in the sky.” — Gilliam. https://cliveandrews.com/2007/02/05/better-than-any-screensaver/

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from Under a Grey Sky, 2012: “Too beautiful to be widely considered an eyesore, it now stands as a monument for all the other struggling seaside towns as it waits for the ever-promised attention and renovations.” — Matt L. https://underagreysky.com/2012/03/05/starlings-on-the-pier-brighton/

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from QueenSpark Books, “Oh! What a Lovely Pier”, 1996: “Several times I saw porpoises basking in the sea. The first time I thought they were whales.” — Daphne M., who worked on the pier from 1956. https://archive.queensparkbooks.org.uk/oh-what-a-lovely-pier/

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from the Argus readers' Facebook group, on the paddling pool by the West Pier: “Spent every day in summer holidays with my boys here... they loved it and felt so safe.” — Pauline Y. https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/18661633.argus-readers-share-memories-growing-brighton/

messages.name: The West Pier Curator
messages.text: Found memory, from Clive A.'s blog, 2007 (the starlings): “It's always different, yet always the same. you can watch it for ages. Better than any screensaver.” — Clive A. https://cliveandrews.com/2007/02/05/better-than-any-screensaver/
